sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Central angle per side?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
the space between two intersecting lines
the amount of turn measured in degrees

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Open the compass to more than half of AB. From A draw an arc above and below AB; from B, with the same opening, draw arcs crossing them. Draw the line through the two crossing points. What has been constructed?
A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 12. What central angle does each side subtend?
